key_insight: Freestream turbulence strongly reshapes a moderate adverse-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer over an airfoil, making the mean flow and near-wall statistics move toward more canonical zero-pressure-gradient behavior.
engineering_relevance: In aerodynamic design and testing, freestream turbulence must be accounted for because it can alter boundary-layer development, skin friction, and separation-related wake structure under realistic adverse pressure gradients.
method: Wind-tunnel experiments on a NACA 0015 airfoil
Angle of attack set to 2° and 4° to vary the pressure gradient
Hotwire measurements taken at x/c = 0.400–0.625 for FST levels from 0.15% to 6%
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic changes in shape factor, skin-friction coefficient, velocity variance, and spectral energy as FST increases, with larger effects at stronger adverse pressure gradients.
watch_item: These findings come from a moderate-APG airfoil case at fixed Reynolds number, so direct transfer to other geometries, stronger APGs, or different Reynolds numbers should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Effect of free-stream turbulence on a moderate adverse pressure gradient turbulent boundary layer developing over an airfoil
